title: Marking criteria for one kind of open-ended item
description: Written before the answer exists. That order is the whole point: criteria decided after reading an answer will be shaped by the answer, and the shaping runs one way, towards accepting it. A rubric is also what the marking subagent receives instead of the teaching transcript, so it has to be complete on its own - it is read by something that does not know the learner, did not see the lesson, and has no way to fill a gap from context.

applies_to.description: What kind of answer this marks, stated so a marker who has seen nothing else can tell whether it is the right rubric.

criteria.description: Each one must be decidable from the answer alone. A criterion that requires knowing what was taught cannot be applied by a marker who did not see the teaching, which is every marker here.

requires.description: What the answer has to contain or do. Written as something observable, not as a quality: 'states when the approximation stops holding', not 'shows good understanding'.

evidence_looks_like.description: What a passing answer would actually say. Present so that a marker deciding this criterion is met has something concrete to compare against, and so that a pass which cannot quote anything resembling this is visibly wrong.

common_miss.description: The way answers usually fail this criterion. Often the most useful line in the rubric: it names the near-miss that reads as correct.

required_for_pass.description: When true, missing this fails the item regardless of everything else. Use for the criteria the item exists to test; without any, a confident answer that misses the point can accumulate enough partial credit to pass.

depth.description: The depth an answer meeting this criterion demonstrates. Lets a verdict say what was actually shown rather than what the item hoped for.

pass_threshold.description: Fraction of weighted criteria needed, on top of every required_for_pass criterion being met. Both conditions, never either.

not_evidence.description: Things that must not be counted as meeting a criterion: restating the question, using the right terms without the reasoning, arriving at the right number by a wrong route, agreeing with something the marker said. Listed because each of these reads as competence.

refuse_to_guess.description: Default true. When the answer is too incomplete to judge, the verdict is that it cannot be judged and why, never a charitable reading. A charitable reading is how an unearned pass enters the record, and once recorded it schedules reviews as though the material were known.
